title: CI perf-smoke: validate perf-canary metrics + alert/dashboard compatibility
creator: Noah Patel
description:
Problem
We’ve had multiple near-misses where perf-canary deploys succeeded but downstream pieces broke:
- metric name/label changes caused dashboards to go red (missing series)
- alert rules failed to evaluate due to schema drift (labels missing / histograms renamed)
- incident-bot payload was present but lacked links because the underlying query panel IDs changed

Given perf-canary is intended to gate rollouts, we need a lightweight CI smoke check that runs on every change to:
- perf-canary (service emitting metrics)
- runtime telemetry fields required for attribution (queueing time / kernel tags)
- observability-pack dashboards/alerts

Goal
Add a small, fast CI job that validates:
1) perf-canary emits the required metric families with the expected label set (within our cardinality guardrails)
2) Grafana dashboards and Prometheus/Alertmanager rules in observability-pack still evaluate against those metrics (no missing series / parse errors)
3) alert-webhook payload formatting remains compatible with incident-bot handler expectations (basic schema check)

Non-goals
- end-to-end performance validation (latency targets) in CI
- full integration test of incident-bot posting to Slack
- validating every region/SKU combination (CI uses a minimal config)

Proposed approach
A) Add a "metrics contract" file to perf-canary repo
- Define required metric names + types + required labels and optional labels
- Example (illustrative, final list in repo):
  - redwood_perf_canary_request_latency_ms (histogram) labels: model, model_version, region, tier, runtime_build, hw_sku
  - redwood_perf_canary_tokens_per_sec (gauge) labels: model, model_version, region, tier, runtime_build, hw_sku
  - redwood_runtime_queueing_time_ms (histogram) labels: model, region, tier, hw_sku
  - redwood_runtime_kernel_id (info/gauge) labels: model, kernel_id, runtime_build
- Enforce a strict allowlist of labels; fail CI if new labels are introduced without updating the contract (prevents accidental cardinality blowups)

B) CI job: "perf-canary-smoke"
- Spin up perf-canary locally in a docker compose / kind environment with:
  - a fake inference endpoint (or a stubbed internal endpoint) that returns deterministic tokens + latencies
  - a local Prometheus scrape target capturing emitted metrics
  - optional: promtool rule evaluation for alert rules (pull in observability-pack rules as artifacts)
- Run for ~2–3 minutes to generate enough samples for time series existence checks
- Assertions:
  - required series exist for a fixed minimal config: 1 model, 1 region, 1 hw_sku
  - label set matches contract (no missing required labels, no extra labels)
  - histogram buckets exist for latency metrics (basic structural check)
  - promtool check passes for alert rules (syntax + evaluation)

C) Dashboard compatibility checks (lightweight)
- Validate JSON dashboards still reference existing metric names using a grep/AST pass:
  - parse dashboard JSON, extract PromQL expressions, ensure metric names referenced exist in the contract
  - do not attempt to render dashboards in CI

D) Alert payload schema check
- Unit test for the webhook payload object emitted by perf-canary regression evaluator:
  - required keys present: model, model_version, observed, baseline, regression_pct, confidence, links
  - links include dashboard URL template placeholders for region/model

Acceptance criteria
- CI fails if a required metric is not emitted or required labels are missing
- CI fails if a new label is introduced on contract-bound metrics without an explicit contract update
- CI fails if promtool detects broken alert rule syntax or missing metric references
- CI fails if any Grafana dashboard query references a metric not present in the contract
- Total runtime <= 6 minutes on standard CI runners
- Documented in README: how to run locally and how to update the contract intentionally

Rollout plan
- Start as non-blocking (informational) for 2–3 days to tune flakes
- Move to required status check for perf-canary + observability-pack repos
- Add release-engineering note: "perf-canary-smoke" must be green before enabling canary in a new region

Risks / notes
- Flakiness: prefer existence/contract checks over threshold-based assertions. Keep minimal runtime.
- Version drift across repos: pin observability-pack rules/dashboards as a CI artifact from the PR branch when possible; otherwise use main with a warning.
- Avoid generating high-cardinality labels in the test harness (match the production label allowlist).

References
- ENG-4873 Define per-model regression metrics (contract source of truth)
- ENG-4877 Observability dashboards for canary
- ENG-4878 Alerting policy and oncall routing
- PR-19212 Emit metrics latency/tokens-per-sec
- PR-19244 Alert webhook payload format

2026-01-16 (Caleb Johnson): Agree. Proposal: keep a metrics_contract.yaml in perf-canary and validate emitted series via local Prometheus scrape. Also run promtool against alert rules in observability-pack.
2026-01-17 (Allison Grant): Please include label allowlist enforcement. We just had a cardinality review; any new label on histograms must be explicit + reviewed.
2026-01-20 (Logan Wright): +1. Make the test only assert existence + schema, not values. Values are noisy in CI. Also watch for histogram bucket naming; promtool is good for syntax but not existence.

2026-01-24 (Caleb Johnson): Implemented draft contract and CI job in perf-canary. Current runtime ~4m30s. Uses stub inference server to generate deterministic token counts. Added promtool check that runs against rules pulled from observability-pack main (temporary until we wire cross-repo artifact).
2026-01-27 (Noah Patel): Looks good. One request: add a lint that extracts metric identifiers from dashboard JSON and compares to contract list. That would have caught the last rename.
2026-01-30 (Caleb Johnson): Added dashboard PromQL scanner (best-effort; handles common patterns). Also added unit test for webhook payload keys and dashboard link templates.
2026-02-03 (Allison Grant): Reviewed. This meets paging hygiene requirements. Please flip from informational to required after 48 hours of green runs.
2026-02-06 (Caleb Johnson): Flipped to required. No flakes observed across 30 runs. Marking Done.
